title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel, comprising the Directors and Senior Executives of the Company. All prohibitions and exceptions in the Policy apply to this tier only.

windows.start_anchor: end of a financial reporting period
windows.end_anchor: day after the preliminary announcement of the half-yearly or annual results
day after the release of the monthly Net Asset Backing Announcement

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate a period of time as a prohibited period under this Policy; the Policy does not state whether such a designation is confidential.

rules.detail: The Policy has no definition of 'dealing' or 'securities' and never mentions derivatives, options, or other financial products created over the Company's shares; it restricts only 'dealing'/'trading' in 'the Company's securities' itself.
No mention of hedging, economic risk, or equity incentive scheme securities anywhere in the Policy.
Prepaid forwards, collars or other monetisation structures are not mentioned.
Absolute ban on short selling of the Company's securities, applying to KMPs at all times (not limited to closed periods).
rules.evidence: KMPs must not engage in short selling of the Company's securities

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not mentioned; the Policy does not define 'securities' to include financial products referencing the Company's shares.
Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Granting a charge, lien, pledge or other security over the Company's securities is not mentioned and there is no dealing definition to sweep it in.
No provision on secured financing or loans secured against the Company's securities.
No minimum holding period, intention test, or short-term dealing restriction is stated.

clearance.evidence: A KMP may be given approval to transact on the Company's securities if application is made in writing in advance to the Board, and only if the Board considers there to be a sufficiently exceptional circumstance that the implementation of the general Policy would produce an inappropriate outcome, and where the KMP is not in possession of any price sensitive information.

exceptions.evidence: Transfers of securities where there is no change in relevant interest
An investment in an entity where the assets of the entity are invested at the discretion of a third party
Responding to a corporate action or offer which has been made to all the Company's security holders of the same class
Transactions conducted between a KMP and a close family member
Transactions which are outside the control of the KMP, including those which result from the application of law.

A KMP may be given approval to transact on the Company's securities if application is made in writing in advance to the Board, and only if the Board considers there to be a sufficiently exceptional circumstance that the implementation of the general Policy would produce an inappropriate outcome, and where the KMP is not in possession of any price sensitive information.

exemption_authority: The Board may approve dealing during a prohibited period in exceptional circumstances where the KMP holds no price sensitive information (5.1-5.2); the Company may also designate additional prohibited periods (3.3). Confidentiality of either is not addressed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no definitions section; it refers only to KMPs dealing/trading/transacting in 'the Company's securities' without defining 'deal', 'securities' or 'relevant interest' beyond the beneficial-interest reference in the transfer exclusion.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express or definitional hook sweeping OTC derivatives, hedging, margin lending or encumbrance into the Policy's restrictions, so on its face a funded collar with a bank is not caught by anything beyond the general insider-information and closed-period rules; this also means the analysis rests on an absence of prohibition rather than a clear permission, which the bank should confirm with the company.

bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP's are not permitted to trade in the Company's Securities during the period from the end of a calendar month until the day after the release of the monthly Net Asset Backing Announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a listed investment company Whitefield issues a monthly NAB announcement, so this closed period recurs every month and materially narrows the windows available to execute, adjust or unwind a collar if entry/settlement is treated as 'trading' in the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy applies only to 'private dealings in Whitefield's issued securities by Key Management Personnel' with no reference to options, rights, or vesting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no unvested/vested-locked distinction to navigate; any WHF shares held by a KMP can be treated as unrestricted for Policy purposes, subject only to the closed periods and the insider information ban.

summary: A funded collar is likely available to a WHF KMP under this Policy, subject to timing. The Policy is narrow: it restricts KMPs (Directors and Senior Executives) only from dealing while holding undisclosed price-sensitive information and from trading during the half-year/annual reporting closed period or the recurring monthly Net Asset Backing closed period (absent Board approval for exceptional circumstances), and separately bans short selling outright. It contains no definitions of 'dealing' or 'securities', and does not mention derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing at all, so a purchased put, written call and a loan secured on the collared shares are not expressly prohibited or brought within scope by any dealing definition. The main practical constraints are that entry, adjustment and unwind should occur outside both closed periods and while the KMP holds no inside information, and that the structure should not resemble short selling of WHF shares themselves. Given the sparseness of the Policy, the bank should have the company confirm in writing that a collar and its secured loan are not treated as 'dealing' before proceeding.
